toc.title: The exam, its scope and how this course works

html:
1What You Will Learn

  • Describe the exam: its length, its two question types and how it is scored
  • Say what the exam guide covers and why you should read the current version
  • Name the four domains and their weights
  • Know who the exam is for and which services it leaves out
  • Use the tags, case, Design Checks and questions of this course

2The exam, its scope and how this course works

Running case

Meet Lantern and Loom

  • Lantern and Loom is a fictional online marketplace for handmade goods, run by a small engineering team
  • It starts as one web server and one database and has to become secure, resilient, fast and affordable
  • Each module follows one decision: who may do what, how it scales, how it survives a failure, how it stays fast, what it costs
  • Your job: design the architecture, and learn why one service fits better than its look-alikes

The Exam at a Glance

  • 65 questions: 50 are scored and 15 are unscored trial questions
  • You cannot tell which are unscored, so treat every question as real
  • 130 minutes in all: about 2 minutes a question
  • Your result is a scaled score from 100 to 1,000, and 720 passes

Exam tip: The 15 unscored questions are not marked on screen, so give every question your full attention.

Question Types and Scoring

  • Multiple choice: one correct answer and three distractors
  • Multiple response: two or more correct answers out of five or more options; the question says how many to choose
  • Distractors are plausible answers that match the topic, so read each option against the requirement
  • An unanswered question counts as wrong, and there is no penalty for guessing
  • Compensatory scoring: you must pass the exam as a whole, not each section

Exam tip: Never leave a question blank: a guess costs nothing and a blank always scores zero.

Booking, Taking and Keeping the Credential [Verify live]

  • Fee: USD 150, with possible extra costs such as exchange rates
  • Delivery: at a Pearson VUE test center or online with a proctor
  • Languages: ten, including English; the Italian version retires after 31 December 2026
  • Valid for 3 years; renew by passing the latest version of the exam or by earning the Solutions Architect Professional certification
  • No formal prerequisites
  • As of 5 November 2026: check AWS's certification page for price, languages and delivery

Exam tip: Fees, languages and renewal rules change; read AWS's page before you book.

The Exam Guide Is Your Scope [Dates]

  • The exam guide lists the domains, weights, task statements and in-scope services
  • This course follows version 1.1, published on 29 October 2026
  • The guide had two versions: 28 August 2026 and 29 October 2026
  • AWS publishes changes about a month before they reach the exam
  • The service list is non-exhaustive and subject to change
  • The guide outranks this course on scope

Exam tip: Read the current exam guide before you book and again in the last week.

Four Domains, Fourteen Task Statements

  • Domain 1, Design Secure Architectures: 30%, three task statements
  • Domain 2, Design Resilient Architectures: 26%, two
  • Domain 3, Design High-Performing Architectures: 24%, five
  • Domain 4, Design Cost-Optimized Architectures: 20%, four

Exam tip: Security and resilience together carry 56 percent of the exam; cost is a fifth.

Who the Exam Is For

  • The exam validates the ability to design solutions based on the AWS Well-Architected Framework
  • The target candidate has at least one year of hands-on experience designing cloud solutions with AWS services
  • Skills tested: design for current needs and future growth, build architectures that are secure, resilient, high-performing and cost-optimized, and review existing solutions
  • Out of scope services include Internet of Things services, Amazon Lightsail, AWS CodeBuild and CodeDeploy, AWS CDK, Amazon GameLift and the Elemental media services

Exam tip: Questions ask you to choose a design for a stated requirement, so learn when to use each service, not only what it is.

How This Course Works

  • 17 modules: this introduction, 14 content modules in the guide's order, a recap and an exam-technique module
  • Each content module has what you will learn, a Lantern and Loom case, Exam Tips, a recap and practice questions
  • A Design Check in each module: a requirement, and the design that fits
  • Slide tags: Beyond the guide, Old name, Verify live, Dates

Independent Course, Official Sources

  • This course is independent: not affiliated with, endorsed or sponsored by Amazon Web Services
  • It shows no AWS logos or service icons; service names appear as text
  • The notes and questions are in our own wording; it uses no AWS exam questions or dumps
  • AWS documentation and the exam guide outrank this course on every fact and rule
  • Limits, prices and service names change: check the source on every Verify-live slide

Exam tip: When this course and the current AWS documentation disagree, the documentation wins.

3Quick Reference Card

  • Study one module, then do its questions; the modules follow the exam guide's order
  • Cover every task statement: the guide does not weight them separately
  • Read the exam guide before you book and again in the last week
  • Answer all 65 questions on the day; never leave one blank
  • This course is independent and educational: the official sources outrank it

Exam tip: Before you book, read AWS's current exam guide and certification page.
